selected_result: Theorem 3.7: probabilistic componentwise backward error for a Gaussian-elimination solution

bibliographic_source.title: A New Approach to Probabilistic Rounding Error Analysis

task_clarification: For A in R^(n x n) and b in R^n, suppose Gaussian elimination under Model 2.1 produces computed factors LHat,UHat and a computed solution xHat to A*x=b.

For every lambda>0, with probability at least Q(lambda,n^3/3+3*n^2/2+7*n/6), there exists DeltaA such that (A+DeltaA)*xHat=b and |DeltaA|<=(3*gammaTilde_n(lambda)+gammaTilde_n(lambda)^2)*|LHat|*|UHat| componentwise.
The source combines LU factorization with both triangular substitutions. The conclusion must refer to the output of that whole computation.
scope_constraints: Keep Model 2.1, the exact polynomial argument of Q, the quadratic gammaTilde coefficient, and the computed-factor scale.
Do not replace the componentwise bound by a normwise or deterministic one.
Do not assume the target perturbed linear system or event as a run hypothesis.
